intent: One choice inside a NativeSelect, shown as its text and submitted as its value.
typical_uses: One entry in a NativeSelect's list of choices

dont_use_when.situation: Item content beyond plain text (an icon, a description, per-option styling)

invariants.text: The option's text content is what the user sees in the picker and what assistive tech announces; `value` is what the form submits and what the select compares its own `value`/`defaultValue` against.

anti_patterns.dont: Preselect this option by setting `selected` on it
anti_patterns.do_instead: Set `defaultValue` or `value` on the surrounding NativeSelect - React warns on `selected`, and the select, not the option, owns the selection state

a11y.by: native-select.test.tsx's option queries - getByRole('option', { name: 'Americas' }) and getByRole('option', { name: 'France' }) - which read an option's announced name from its text content

bad.title: An option with no select around it
bad.why: An <option> holds no state of its own - the surrounding <select> owns the selection - so outside one it is inert markup with no picker to appear in.
